changes.sourceText: Yours, LORD, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, LORD, and you are exalted as head above all.

changes.nextContext: Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGodの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ダビデは神に感謝し、その栄光ある名をたたえます。
changes.sourceText: Now therefore, our God, we thank you and praise your glorious name.
changes.previousContext: Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!
changes.nextContext: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGodの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ダビデは、神殿建設のために用意した蓄えもすべて神の御手から来たもので、神ご自身のものだと告白します。
changes.sourceText: LORD our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own.
changes.previousContext: For we are strangers before you and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow, and there is no remaining.
changes.nextContext: I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGodの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ダビデは、神が人の心を試し、正しさを喜ばれると述べ、自分と民が喜んでささげたと語ります。
changes.sourceText: I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.
changes.previousContext: LORD our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own.
changes.nextContext: LORD, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you;

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGodの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ダビデは、アブラハム、イサク、イスラエルの神である主に、民の心の志を保ち、ご自分へ向けて整えてくださるよう願います。
changes.sourceText: LORD, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you;
changes.previousContext: I know also, my God, that you try the heart and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you.
changes.nextContext: and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”

changes.afterTextJa: ダビデが会衆に主をほめたたえるよう呼びかけると、人々は主を祝福し、頭を垂れて主と王の前にひれ伏します。
changes.sourceText: Then David said to all the assembly, “Now bless the LORD your God!” All the assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers, and bowed down their heads and prostrated themselves before the LORD and the king.
changes.previousContext: and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”

changes.afterTextJa: 翌日、イスラエル全体のために雄牛、雄羊、小羊各千頭などが主にささげられます。
changes.sourceText: They sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the next day after that day, even one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel,

changes.nextContext: and ate and drank before the LORD on that day with great gladness. They made Solomon the son of David king the second time, and anointed him before the LORD to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGodの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: その日、人々は主の前で喜びながら食べ飲みし、ソロモンを再び王とし、ツァドクを祭司にします。

changes.nextContext: Then Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.

changes.afterTextJa: ソロモンはダビデに代わって主の王座に座り、栄え、イスラエル全体が彼に従います。
changes.sourceText: Then Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeyed him.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGodの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: 主はイスラエル全体の前でソロモンを大いに高め、先代の王たちにまさる王威を与えます。
changes.sourceText: The LORD magnified Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gave to him such royal majesty as had not been on any king before him in Israel.
changes.previousContext: All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of King David submitted themselves to Solomon the king.
changes.nextContext: Now David the son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGershonの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: レビの子として、ゲルションはケハトとメラリと共に系譜に挙げられます。
changes.sourceText: The sons of Levi: Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
changes.previousContext: Jehozadak went into captivity when the LORD carried Judah and Jerusalem away by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
changes.nextContext: These are the names of the sons of Gershom: Libni and Shimei.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGadの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ダビデはガドに、憐れみ深い主の手に委ね、人の手には渡されないことを願ったと答えます。
changes.sourceText: David said to Gad, “I am in distress. Let me fall, I pray, into the LORD’s hand, for his mercies are very great. Don’t let me fall into man’s hand.”
changes.previousContext: either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or else three days of the sword of the LORD, even pestilence in the land, and the LORD’s angel destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now therefore consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.’”
changes.nextContext: So the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGadの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: 主の使いはガドに、ダビデがオルナンの打ち場へ上り、主のための祭壇を築くよう告げます。
changes.sourceText: Then the LORD’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
changes.previousContext: David said to God, “Isn’t it I who commanded the people to be counted? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, O LORD my God, be against me and against my father’s house; but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”
changes.nextContext: David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spoke in the LORD’s name.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもGadの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ダビデ王の生涯の記録は、先見者サムエル、預言者ナタン、先見者ガドの書にも記されています。
changes.sourceText: Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer,
changes.previousContext: He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
changes.nextContext: with all his reign and his might, and the events that involved him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the lands.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもHadadの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ハダドが死ぬと、マスレカ出身のサムラが後を継いで王となります。
changes.sourceText: Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
changes.previousContext: Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith.
changes.nextContext: Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned in his place.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもHanunの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: アンモン人の長たちはハヌンに、ダビデの慰問使節は父への敬意でなく偵察に来たのではないかと疑いを述べます。
changes.sourceText: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his servants come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?”
changes.previousContext: David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun to comfort him.
changes.nextContext: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved them, and cut off their garments in the middle at their buttocks, and sent them away.

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもHilkiahの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: 系譜は、アザルヤの父ヒルキヤを、メシュラム、ツァドク、メライヨテ、アヒトブへとつなげ、アザルヤを神の家の責任者と記します。
changes.sourceText: and Azariah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the ruler of God’s house;
changes.previousContext: Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
changes.nextContext: and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah; and Maasai the son of Adiel, the son of Jahzerah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Meshillemith, the son of Immer;

changes.beforeText: 後の記載でもHebronの名が挙がります。
changes.afterTextJa: ヘブロンの子として、コラ、タプア、レケム、シェマの四人が挙げられます。
changes.sourceText: The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
changes.previousContext: The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel were Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron.
changes.nextContext: Shema became the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem became the father of Shammai.
